gaps.concept: High FSH with low estradiol indicates ovarian insufficiency; low or normal FSH with low estradiol indicates hypothalamic or pituitary suppression.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes ovarian failure from central causes in an amenorrhea hormone panel. [ASRM](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/)

gaps.concept: An FMR1 premutation, autoimmunity, chemotherapy, or pelvic radiation can cause primary ovarian insufficiency before age 40.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the cause of amenorrhea with elevated FSH in a young patient. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/primary-ovarian-insufficiency)

gaps.concept: Turner syndrome causes 45,X gonadal dysgenesis with streak ovaries, low estrogen, elevated FSH, short stature, and an intact uterus.
gaps.why_tested: Explains primary amenorrhea without breast development in a short adolescent. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/01/mullerian-agenesis-diagnosis-management-and-treatment)

gaps.concept: Kallmann syndrome results from failed migration of GnRH neurons and causes anosmia with low gonadotropins and delayed puberty.
gaps.why_tested: Links absent smell to hypogonadotropic primary amenorrhea.

gaps.concept: MRKH syndrome is Müllerian agenesis in a 46,XX patient with ovaries, normal breasts and pubic hair, absent uterus, and possible renal anomalies.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes MRKH from androgen insensitivity when imaging shows no uterus. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/01/mullerian-agenesis-diagnosis-management-and-treatment)

gaps.concept: Complete androgen insensitivity causes a 46,XY phenotype with testes, absent uterus, scant pubic hair, male-range testosterone, and breast development through aromatization.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes androgen insensitivity from MRKH in a patient with primary amenorrhea. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/01/mullerian-agenesis-diagnosis-management-and-treatment)

gaps.concept: An imperforate hymen causes cyclic pelvic pain, hematocolpos, and a bulging bluish membrane despite normal breast development.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies an outflow obstruction in an adolescent with primary amenorrhea. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/01/mullerian-agenesis-diagnosis-management-and-treatment)

gaps.concept: Elevated prolactin suppresses GnRH, lowering LH and FSH; galactorrhea with amenorrhea suggests hyperprolactinemia.
gaps.why_tested: Explains anovulation in a patient with spontaneous milk discharge. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/en-ca/professional/endocrine-and-metabolic-disorders/pituitary-disorders/prolactinoma)

gaps.concept: Primary hypothyroidism raises TRH, which stimulates prolactin release and can cause amenorrhea with galactorrhea.
gaps.why_tested: Links elevated TSH and prolactin in a patient with menstrual loss. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/en-ca/professional/endocrine-and-metabolic-disorders/pituitary-disorders/prolactinoma)

gaps.concept: Dopamine-blocking drugs, especially antipsychotics and metoclopramide, can raise prolactin and cause amenorrhea.
gaps.why_tested: Makes medication history decisive in a galactorrhea vignette. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/amenorrhea)

gaps.concept: Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary infarction after severe hemorrhage; failure to lactate can precede amenorrhea.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies pituitary failure after postpartum bleeding.

gaps.concept: Asherman syndrome is intrauterine scarring, often after postpartum curettage, causing secondary amenorrhea or infertility.
gaps.why_tested: Connects uterine instrumentation to absent menses despite preserved ovarian function. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/abnormal-uterine-bleeding)

gaps.concept: No progestin-withdrawal bleed suggests low estrogen or damaged endometrium/outflow obstruction; no bleed after estrogen-progestin challenge favors the latter.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets sequential challenge tests in secondary amenorrhea. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/amenorrhea)

gaps.concept: During lactation, elevated prolactin suppresses GnRH and ovulation, producing physiologic amenorrhea.
gaps.why_tested: Explains absent menses in a breastfeeding patient.

gaps.concept: In PCOS, elevated LH and hyperinsulinemia stimulate ovarian theca cells to produce excess androgens.
gaps.why_tested: Asks for the hormone-producing cell or mechanism behind hyperandrogenism. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2019/10/screening-and-management-of-the-hyperandrogenic-adolescent)

gaps.concept: Hyperinsulinemia suppresses hepatic sex hormone-binding globulin, increasing free testosterone despite modest total testosterone elevation.
gaps.why_tested: Explains hirsutism when total testosterone is only mildly elevated. [ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2019/10/screening-and-management-of-the-hyperandrogenic-adolescent)

gaps.concept: PCOS follicles arrest before ovulation, producing numerous small peripheral follicles rather than mature ovulatory follicles.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound.

gaps.concept: Peripheral aromatization of androgens produces estrone in PCOS, while absent ovulation prevents cyclic progesterone secretion.
gaps.why_tested: Explains persistent endometrial proliferation in a patient with irregular menses.

gaps.concept: Letrozole inhibits aromatase, lowering estrogen feedback and raising FSH to promote follicular development.
gaps.why_tested: Asks how the listed first-line PCOS ovulation drug works.

gaps.concept: Spironolactone blocks androgen receptors; hyperkalemia and feminization of a male fetus are relevant adverse effects.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the mechanism or adverse effect of a hirsutism prescription.

gaps.concept: Anovulatory bleeding follows prolonged estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation without progesterone, causing irregular, sometimes heavy, shedding.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes irregular anovulatory bleeding from heavy but regular ovulatory bleeding. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/abnormal-uterine-bleeding)

gaps.concept: Heavy bleeding beginning at menarche, especially with easy bruising or epistaxis, suggests von Willebrand disease.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies a coagulopathy from an adolescent abnormal-bleeding history. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/abnormal-uterine-bleeding)

gaps.concept: Leiomyomas are estrogen-responsive benign smooth-muscle tumors with firm, whorled cut surfaces; submucosal lesions can cause heavy bleeding and infertility.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies fibroids from an enlarged irregular uterus, imaging, or gross pathology. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/uterine-fibroids/uterine-fibroids)

gaps.concept: Adenomyosis consists of endometrial glands and stroma within myometrium, producing heavy painful menses and a diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes adenomyosis from discrete fibroids or extrauterine endometriosis. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/en-ca/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/miscellaneous-gynecologic-disorders/uterine-adenomyosis)

gaps.concept: Endometriosis has ectopic endometrial glands and stroma; progressive dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia, infertility, powder-burn implants, or chocolate cysts are clues.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies endometriosis from symptoms, laparoscopy, or ovarian pathology. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/endometriosis/endometriosis)

gaps.concept: Continuous GnRH agonist exposure suppresses gonadotropins and estrogen in endometriosis; hypoestrogenic hot flashes and bone loss may follow.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the mechanism and adverse effects of hormonal suppression for endometriosis.

gaps.concept: Endometrial polyps can cause intermenstrual bleeding; histology shows glands in fibrous stroma with thick-walled vessels.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies a focal uterine lesion on ultrasound or biopsy. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557824/)

gaps.concept: Endometrial hyperplasia shows crowded glands with an increased gland-to-stroma ratio; cytologic atypia increases malignant potential.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets biopsy after prolonged anovulation and abnormal bleeding. [NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK560693/)

gaps.concept: Pregnancy must also be excluded in reproductive-age abnormal uterine bleeding, including bleeding that appears to be a menstrual period.
gaps.why_tested: Makes a pregnancy test the first diagnostic step in a bleeding vignette. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/abnormal-uterine-bleeding)

gaps.concept: Transvaginal ultrasound assesses structural causes of abnormal bleeding; endometrial sampling assesses malignancy risk in older or high-risk patients.
gaps.why_tested: Selects the diagnostic test for a structural lesion or concerning endometrial bleeding. [Merck](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/abnormal-uterine-bleeding/abnormal-uterine-bleeding)

gaps.concept: A midluteal progesterone level above 3 ng/mL supports recent ovulation; urinary LH kits detect the preceding surge.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets ovulation testing during infertility evaluation. [ASRM](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/)

gaps.concept: Low anti-Müllerian hormone or a low antral follicle count suggests diminished ovarian reserve.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets ovarian-reserve tests in a patient with infertility. [ASRM](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/)

gaps.concept: Free intraperitoneal contrast spill on hysterosalpingography indicates tubal patency; absent spill suggests obstruction.
gaps.why_tested: Requires interpretation of the named infertility imaging test. [ASRM](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/)

gaps.concept: Ovarian hyperstimulation after gonadotropins or hCG involves VEGF-mediated vascular leakage, causing enlarged ovaries, ascites, hemoconcentration, and thrombosis risk.
gaps.why_tested: Explains abdominal distension and hemoconcentration after ovulation induction. [ASRM](https://integration.asrm.org/globalassets/_asrm/practice-guidance/practice-guidelines/pdf/prevention_and_treatment_of_moderate_to_severe_ohss.pdf)
